note: Latin letters that aren't a base letter plus an accent, so decomposing a word doesn't take their mark off. 'folds' is what each reads as without diacritics (ł as l, ß as ss, þ as th), applied before the marks are dropped and again to what decomposition leaves; İ is here because lower-casing leaves it. 'secondForms' are second spellings some languages write, by language: German ü ö ä as ue oe ae; Danish and Norwegian ø as oe and å as aa; Serbian and Croatian đ as dj. A word gets one more reading per group whose letters it has, and one with every such group together (Åström reads as astrom, astroem, aastrom and aastroem). Keys are single lower-case letters as the normaliser leaves them.
